headline: Commission on Persons with Disabilities

meeting.summary: The commission heard an ethics briefing, voted to create an accessibility concern tracker, and will put a post-hurricane review on its next agenda.
meeting.recap: The Commission on Persons with Disabilities met September 10, in person and by video.[[0:00:30]] Commissioners approved earlier meeting minutes by voice vote.[[0:14:43]] The ethics director gave a training on rules about gifts, financial interests and confidential information.[[0:17:17]] The director said the ethics office gave 180 formal advisory opinions in its first year.[[0:32:43]] The director asked members to call at least three business days before a vote with ethics questions.[[0:37:04]] A commissioner said there was no commission action yet on a request about accessible state trails.[[0:58:59]] The chair said the commission had no response yet on an accessibility issue at the Maui County Building.[[1:00:08]] The chair will personally contact public works and the management director about it.[[1:02:22]] Special Fair Day is October 2nd.[[1:12:24]] A commissioner said the county's ClickFix system has no category just for ADA (disability access) concerns.[[1:19:57]] A motion was made to let the chair send a disability accessibility letter; no vote was heard.[[1:32:22]] A commissioner proposed asking the emergency management agency how the recent hurricane affected people with disabilities.[[1:41:12]] That request will be placed on the next meeting's agenda.[[1:43:10]]
decided: The commission approved the minutes of an earlier meeting by voice vote.
A motion to give the chair authority to send a letter on disability accessibility was made and seconded, but no vote was heard in the recording.
meeting.next: The chair said they will get back to the commission on the building issue even though they will miss the next meeting. A post-hurricane review request will be placed on the next meeting's agenda.

moments.q: "It just really needs to be dealt with."
